subject: math
title: Add and Subtract Within 100
seo_title: Grade 2 Addition and Subtraction Within 100 Worksheets: 2-Digit Regrouping, Base-Ten Blocks and Word Problems
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 worksheets for adding and subtracting 2-digit numbers within 100: base-ten blocks, regrouping, subtracting from tens, missing numbers, adding three or four numbers and word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Add or subtract the ones first, then the tens. 10 ones make 1 ten.
key_sub: Adding: if the ones make 10 or more, regroup 1 ten. Subtracting: if the top ones digit is smaller, trade 1 ten for 10 ones. Check a subtraction by adding back.
body_html:
Tens and ones

A 2-digit number has tens and ones. 34 is 3 tens and 4 ones. To add, put the tens together and put the ones together.

10 ones make a new ten

If the ones add up to 10 or more, regroup: trade 10 ones for 1 ten. In columns, write the ones digit and put a small 1 on top of the tens.

Make a ten

What is 38 + 25?

38 needs 2 more to make 40. Take 2 from 25 to get 23. Now add 40 + 23.

Answer: 63

Subtract with regrouping

Start with the ones. If the top digit is smaller, trade 1 ten for 10 ones. Cross out the tens digit and write 1 less.

Count up

What is 60 − 27?

Start at 27. 27 + 3 = 30. 30 + 30 = 60. You counted up 3 + 30.

Answer: 33

Add three or four numbers

Look for ones that make 10 and add them first. You can add in any order.

Look for a ten

What is 26 + 35 + 14?

6 + 4 = 10, so 26 + 14 = 40. Then 40 + 35 = 75.

Answer: 75

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the new ten: 46 + 37 = 73Write the small 1 on top of the tens and add it
Writing 13 in the ones: 46 + 37 = 713Only one digit goes in each column. Regroup the ten
Taking the small digit from the big one: 52 − 27 = 35Always take the bottom digit from the top. Regroup when the top is smaller
Regrouping but not crossing out: 63 − 28 = 45When you trade 1 ten, the tens digit gets 1 smaller
Skipping a number when adding four numbersTouch each number as you add it

faq.q: How do you teach 2-digit addition with regrouping?
faq.a: Start with base-ten blocks: add the ones, and when there are 10 or more, trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Then show the same steps in columns, with a small 1 written on top of the tens.

faq.q: How do you subtract 2-digit numbers with regrouping, like 52 − 27?
faq.a: Start with the ones. 2 − 7 does not work, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Now there are 4 tens: 4 − 2 = 2. The answer is 25.

faq.q: How can my child check a subtraction answer?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number that was taken away. For 52 − 27 = 25, check 25 + 27 = 52. If you get the starting number, the answer is right.
It is the Common Core standard for Grade 2: fluently add and subtract within 100 using place value and the link between addition and subtraction. Standard 2.NBT.B.6 adds up to four 2-digit numbers.

sets.title: Subtract from tens, missing numbers and checking

items.q: What is 100 − 46?
items.e: 100 is 10 tens. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: now 9 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 54. Check: 54 + 46 = 100. Or count up: 46 + 4 = 50, then 50 + 50 = 100. 4 + 50 = 54.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 0 − 3 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 3 = 7. Tens: 8 − 2 = 6. Answer: 67. Check: 67 + 23 = 90. Or count up: 23 + 7 = 30, then 30 + 60 = 90. 7 + 60 = 67.

items.q: What is 80 − 19?
items.e: Ones: 0 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 9 = 1. Tens: 7 − 1 = 6. Answer: 61. Check: 61 + 19 = 80. Or count up: 19 + 1 = 20, then 20 + 60 = 80. 1 + 60 = 61.

items.q: Emma says 63 − 28 = 45. Is she right?
items.e: Check by adding: 45 + 28 = 73, not 63. So 45 is wrong. Ones: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 28 = 63.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 28 + ☐ = 77
items.e: Use subtraction: 77 − 28 = ☐. Ones: 7 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 17 − 8 = 9. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 49. Check: 28 + 49 = 77.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 39 = 95
items.e: Use subtraction: 95 − 39 = ☐. Ones: 5 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 15 − 9 = 6. Tens: 8 − 3 = 5. Answer: 56. Check: 56 + 39 = 95.

items.q: Zoe found 72 − 35 = 37. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 37 + 35 = 72. You get back 72, so the answer is right.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 39 = 74
items.e: Use subtraction: 74 − 39 = ☐. Ones: 4 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 14 − 9 = 5. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 39 = 74.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 27 + ☐ = 81
items.e: Use subtraction: 81 − 27 = ☐. Ones: 1 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 11 − 7 = 4. Tens: 7 − 2 = 5. Answer: 54. Check: 27 + 54 = 81.

items.q: Owen says 91 − 56 = 35. Is he right?
items.e: Check by adding: 35 + 56 = 91. You get back 91, so he is right. Ones: 1 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 11 − 6 = 5. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. Answer: 35.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 0 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 6 − 5 = 1. Answer: 12. Check: 12 + 58 = 70. Or count up: 58 + 2 = 60, then 60 + 10 = 70. 2 + 10 = 12.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 62 − ☐ = 28
items.e: Think: 62 take away what number leaves 28? Find 62 − 28. Ones: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 34. Check: 62 − 34 = 28.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 66 − ☐ = 19
items.e: Think: 66 take away what number leaves 19? Find 66 − 19. Ones: 6 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 16 − 9 = 7. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 47. Check: 66 − 47 = 19.

items.q: What is 60 − 49?
items.e: Ones: 0 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 9 = 1. Tens: 5 − 4 = 1. Answer: 11. Check: 11 + 49 = 60. Or count up: 49 + 1 = 50, then 50 + 10 = 60. 1 + 10 = 11.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 17 = 33
items.e: Use subtraction: 33 − 17 = ☐. Ones: 3 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 16. Check: 16 + 17 = 33.

items.q: Noah found 81 − 47 = 34. Which addition checks his answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 34 + 47 = 81. You get back 81, so the answer is right.

items.q: Ben says 74 − 38 = 44. Is he right?
items.e: Check by adding: 44 + 38 = 82, not 74. So 44 is wrong. Ones: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 14 − 8 = 6. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. Answer: 36. Check: 36 + 38 = 74.

items.q: Ava found 64 − 29 = 35. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 35 + 29 = 64. You get back 64, so the answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 44. Check: 44 + 26 = 70. Or count up: 26 + 4 = 30, then 30 + 40 = 70. 4 + 40 = 44.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 91 − ☐ = 46
items.e: Think: 91 take away what number leaves 46? Find 91 − 46. Ones: 1 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 11 − 6 = 5. Tens: 8 − 4 = 4. Answer: 45. Check: 91 − 45 = 46.

sets.title: Add three or four numbers and word problems

items.q: What is 12 + 38 + 18?
items.e: Look for ones that make 10: 2 + 8 = 10. So 12 + 18 = 30. Then 30 + 38 = 68.

items.q: What is 24 + 31 + 16?
items.e: Look for ones that make 10: 4 + 6 = 10. So 24 + 16 = 40. Then 40 + 31 = 71.

items.q: What is 11 + 26 + 29?
items.e: Look for ones that make 10: 1 + 9 = 10. So 11 + 29 = 40. Then 40 + 26 = 66.

items.e: Ones: 6 + 6 + 1 + 2 = 15. Write 5 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6, plus the regrouped 1 ten = 7. Answer: 75. Remember to add all 4 numbers.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Ones: 4 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 11. Write 1 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 5, plus the regrouped 1 ten = 6. Answer: 61. Remember to add all 4 numbers.

items.e: Ones: 8 + 4 + 7 + 3 = 22. Write 2 and regroup 2 tens. Tens: 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 7, plus the regrouped 2 tens = 9. Answer: 92. Remember to add all 4 numbers.

items.q: Ruby has 38 stickers. Her friend gives her 25 more. How many stickers does Ruby have now?
items.e: Getting more means add. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13. Write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 63.

items.q: A bus has 52 seats. 27 children get on, and each child takes a seat. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Take the full seats away from all the seats: subtract. Ones: 2 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 25. Check: 25 + 27 = 52.

items.q: Jack picks 64 apples. He gives away 29 of them. How many apples are left?
items.e: Giving away means subtract. Ones: 4 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 14 − 9 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 29 = 64.

items.q: Maya read 23 pages on Monday, 18 pages on Tuesday and 31 pages on Wednesday. How many pages did she read in all?
items.e: Add all three days. Ones: 3 + 8 + 1 = 12. Write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6, plus the regrouped 1 ten = 7. Answer: 72.

items.q: The class has 45 crayons. They need 80 crayons. How many more crayons do they need?
items.e: Find the missing part: 45 + ☐ = 80. Count up: 45 + 5 = 50, then 50 + 30 = 80. 5 + 30 = 35. Check: 45 + 35 = 80.

items.q: Luis has 71 cents. Leo has 46 cents. How many more cents does Luis have than Leo?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: subtract. Ones: 1 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 11 − 6 = 5. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. Answer: 25. Check: 25 + 46 = 71.

items.q: A garden has 17 red flowers, 26 yellow flowers, 14 pink flowers and 22 white flowers. How many flowers are there?
items.e: Add all 4 colors. Ones: 7 + 6 + 4 + 2 = 19. Write 9 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 6, plus the regrouped 1 ten = 7. Answer: 79.

items.q: Some birds sit in a tree. 18 birds fly away. Now 35 birds are left. How many birds were in the tree at first?
items.e: The birds that left plus the birds that stayed make all the birds: add. Ones: 5 + 8 = 13. Write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 1 + 1 = 5. Answer: 53. Check: 53 − 18 = 35.

items.q: Kai has 90 cents. He buys a pencil for 36 cents. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Spending money means subtract. Ones: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 8 − 3 = 5. Answer: 54. Check: 54 + 36 = 90.

items.q: A bakery makes 48 muffins in the morning and 37 muffins in the afternoon. How many muffins does it make in all?
items.e: In all means add. Ones: 8 + 7 = 15. Write 5 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Answer: 85.
